title: Crash for --compilation_mode in transition

labels.name: P2
labels.description: We'll consider working on this in future. (Assignee optional)

labels.name: team-Configurability
labels.description: platforms, toolchains, cquery, select(), config transitions

body:
### Description of the problem

`//command_line_option:compilation_mode` exposes a Java class when used as input in a transition, not a string. It is possible to set it to a string as output, but not to read the input.

The same problem also applies for `//command_line_option:run_under` and possibly more.

I would prefer a quick fix for `compilation_mode` whereas `run_under` is not such a big problem for me (just annoying).

### Bugs: what's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.

```
touch WORKSPACE

cat <<EOF > BUILD.bazel
load(":rules.bzl", "rule_with_transition")

rule_with_transition(
    name = "my_target",
)
EOF

cat <<EOF > rules2.bzl
def _my_transition_impl(settings, attr):
    print(settings)
    return dict(settings)

inputs_and_outputs = [
    "//command_line_option:cpu",
    "//command_line_option:compilation_mode",
    "//command_line_option:platform_suffix",
]

my_transition = transition(
    implementation = _my_transition_impl,
    inputs = inputs_and_outputs,
    outputs = inputs_and_outputs,
)

def _rule_impl(ctx):
    pass

rule_with_transition = rule(
    implementation = _rule_impl,
    cfg = my_transition,
    attrs = {
        "_whitelist_function_transition": attr.label(default = "@bazel_tools//tools/whitelists/function_transition_whitelist"),
    },
)
EOF

bazel build :my_target
```

### What operating system are you running Bazel on?

Linux (Ubuntu 17.04)

### What's the output of `bazel info release`?

`release 2.0.0`

###  Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

GitHub issues: https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues
- Nothing found.
